name: Professor X
bio: Telepath, founder of the X-Men and of the school that bears his name. His dream of human–mutant coexistence is the moral axis of the franchise, and nearly every relationship he has is shaped by how far he is willing to bend ethics in service of it. The Krakoan era made him a head of state and finally put him and Magneto on the same side.

target.name: Magneto
target.real_name: Max Eisenhardt (long known as Erik Lehnsherr)

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Silver Age (Lee/Kirby/Thomas)
era.description: X-Men #1 (1963) through the original run's cancellation at #66. The first five students and the founding Xavier/Magneto conflict.

relationships.label: Friends turned ideological rivals
relationships.summary: The founding conflict of the X-Men. They met as young men in Israel (shown in flashback in Uncanny X-Men #161, 1982), bonded over being mutants, and split over whether coexistence with humans was possible. Every subsequent decade restages the argument; the Krakoan era finally put them on the same council.

events.note: Magneto attacks Cape Citadel; the X-Men's first mission is against Xavier's old friend.
Flashback: Charles and Erik meet in Haifa, fight Baron Strucker together, and part over ideology.
Xavier, dying, hands Magneto the school and the New Mutants.
Fatal Attractions prelude; Magneto returns to Asteroid M and dies (apparently) in the fall.
Xavier and Magneto co-found the mutant nation of Krakoa.

relationships.label: Favourite son to patricide
relationships.summary: Xavier's first and most loyal student. The relationship curdled as Scott learned how much Xavier had hidden (Deadly Genesis, 2006), and ended when a Phoenix-possessed Scott killed Xavier. Krakoa, with Xavier resurrected, treated it as a wound neither wanted to discuss.

events.note: Scott is Xavier's field leader from the first mission.
Scott learns Xavier erased his memory of a lost team and expels him from the mansion.

relationships.label: Mentor, with a buried complication
relationships.summary: Xavier trained Jean's telepathy from childhood. X-Men #3 (1964) briefly gave him secret romantic feelings for her, a thread later writers abandoned and then treated as evidence of his ethical blind spots.

events.note: A thought balloon reveals Xavier's attraction to Jean; it is never pursued.
Jean's Phoenix return; Xavier's role in suppressing her power earlier is part of the backstory.
